changes: NumberKey result uses the private numberKeyColumn carrier; NumberPrimary/NumberLookupKey aliases preserve reads and mapping roles but omit Increment/Decrement. Twelve value/pointer snapshot entries removed; one signature replaced.
No new Query/Table/column method names. Plan aliases expose existing non-generic query.Plan/PlanNode surface.

docs_notes: CreateEach runs one ordinary creation lifecycle per input in an atomic bounded batch. FirstOrCreate/UpdateOrCreate lock the first primary-ordered match, default omitted stored inputs from unambiguous equality/scopes, skip retrieval, verify created membership, and rely on unique constraints without retry. Mutators need explicit input.

CreateOrFirst inserts in a child savepoint before lookup. Only its own table-index unique violation after confirmed savepoint rollback can return a matching competitor. Hook/observer/codec failures and uncertainty are returned without retry; snapshot isolation may hide the competitor. Internal hydration skips Retrieved.

PruneBatch physically prunes ordinary models; ForcePruneBatch requires the exact Users.Soft token. Both preserve filters/scopes/visibility and lock bounded candidates. mass=false runs per-model lifecycle; mass=true explicitly skips hooks/observers/audit. Register with prune.ORMModel/ORMSoftModel.

Explain plans; ExplainAnalyze executes. Locked/transaction variants require *database.Tx. Projections/scalars/sets use existing rows.Read* adapters; cursor variants retain canonical ordering without a page boundary. Formatting is redacted; explicit plan JSON/Root snapshots can expose server predicates.

Ordinary Number and NullableNumber Increment/Decrement retain D12 positive finite magnitudes and AtMost/AtLeast guards. NumberPrimary, NumberLookupKey and NumberKey results no longer expose Increment/Decrement. Stored reads, ordering and primary insert mappings remain available. Managed timestamps and Input* fields cannot be numeric adjustment targets.
No persisted schema, manifest, OpenAPI, TypeScript or dependency change. No new Query/Table/column method names. Shared lead-owned documentation was not edited.

CreateOrFirst recovery requires complete server schema, table and constraint metadata matching the resolved target. Custom adapters that omit metadata retain the original violation instead of recovering.

AfterCommit failures retain committed outcome and original cause without invoking application error formatting. Schema/Table metadata are explicit database.Error accessors, omitted from routine formatting and diagnostic output.

review_fixes: CreateOrFirst is a typed package function. Both query.InsertOrFirst and ORM share ormcore.InsertFailure/InsertRows/OwnInsertConflict: statement-only provenance, concrete child TxRolledBack before recovery, bounded full error-graph uncertainty checks, own-table unique-index lookup, no retries and no retrieval hooks. Outer unknown commits retain a typed reconciliation candidate.

Explain compilation, execution and decode failures use lifecore.Failure inside the shared isolated callback. Old query and ORM/rows regressions assert redacted Error/%v/%+v/%#v and errors.Is/As identity; compilation failures send no SQL.

UpdateOrCreate and UpdateEach draft errors use lifecore.Failure before isolation. The old shared modelUpdateMutation and new atomicModels owner also redact before callback formatting. Prune/CreateEach reuse atomicModels; explain variants reuse the shared explain owner.

Conflict provenance retains PostgreSQL SchemaName/TableName through database.Detail and Error. OwnInsertConflict requires nonempty schema/table/constraint and checks them against the destination relation resolved by to_regclass, joining pg_class and pg_namespace. Missing/mismatched identity fails closed. PostgreSQL sources cover identical table/index names across schemas through a trigger for both old query and ORM.

The transaction owner wraps each returned AfterCommit error in the existing database.Error with AfterCommitFailed/Committed before callback isolation formats it. The final aggregate uses the same owner. Direct transaction and real generated local-hook/observer regressions prove Error is never invoked, even when it would panic or Goexit, and errors.Is/As retain identity. No generator/generated-output changes.
